## Summary

Generalized the `@types` fallback so it's not hardcoded to react specifically. Following TDD:

- **RED**: wrote a test calling a not-yet-existing `resolve_package_types_file` against this repo's real `node_modules` — real `react` (exports-only, no types), real `@types/react` present.
- **GREEN**: implemented it as a thin wrapper around `resolve_dts()` — try primary resolution, and only if the result isn't actually a `.d.ts`/`.d.mts`/`.d.cts` file, retry against `@types/<mangled-name>`.
- **Extra edge-case coverage** caught something real along the way: my first "happy path" test picked `class-variance-authority` as a "resolves its own types cleanly" example, and it failed — not because my fix was wrong, but because `resolve_dts` has a *separate* quirk (prefers `import`/`require` conditions over `types` when a package's exports mix them in one object, which `@types/react` doesn't do but CVA does). Swapped the test to resolve `@types/react` directly, which cleanly isolates the primary path with no ambiguity.
- 103 unit tests + 8 snapshot tests pass, clippy clean, `cargo fmt` applied by the pre-commit hook (re-staged and recommitted, per the established pattern in this repo).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is a good example of why "read the source and reason about it" isn't a substitute for actually running the code, twice over in this same fix: my first read of `resolve_dts()`'s source led me to expect it would work correctly once called with the bare package name, and testing proved that wrong (the exports-shortcut bug). Then my *test's own premise* — that CVA was a clean "no fallback needed" example — was also wrong, for a third, different reason. Three separate false assumptions in one small feature, each only caught by actually executing something and looking at the real output.

I traced why RDT showed `rdt=0` for every Chakra/Mantine/MUI/Radix/React Aria component in the comparison, and it's not a coverage gap — **`run-react-docgen-typescript.ts` explicitly filters out `.d.ts` fixtures** (`fixtures.ts:45` / `.filter(f => !f.isDts)`) because RDT's parser needs a real component (a function/expression that *uses* a props type), not a bare type-declaration file. Checking what's actually on disk:

- **chakra, mantine, mui, radix, react-aria — all `.d.ts`-only.** RDT never runs against them at all. Every "coverage %" and "ours-only" list I reported for these last time was just *our own output alone*, with no comparison happening.
- **Only shadcn (3 files), panda (1 file), and rdt-compat (9 files we wrote ourselves) get a genuine two-tool comparison.** That's a narrow, partly self-selected slice — `rdt-compat` was authored specifically to probe gaps we already knew about.

It directly explains *why* your instinct to find real library repos matters: we need actual `.tsx` component source from real design systems, not just their published `@types`-style `.d.ts` declarations, or RDT structurally can't participate in the comparison at all.

All four fixtures are in and verified against real RDT. Here's the full picture.

## The headline number

On **unmodified, real-world code** from four separate design systems, our tool would have silently produced **zero components** for 4 of the 5 sampled components (Fluent Button, Base UI MenuRoot, Base UI MenuTrigger, and Ark UI's Select as originally authored) — not degraded output, just invisible. RDT correctly extracted all of them (303, 15, 293, and 314 props respectively). That's the honest "embarrassing gap" signal you were looking for, and it's real — none of our existing 8 fixtures exercised the patterns that triggered it.

## Root causes — 4 distinct bugs, but really 2 high-value fixes

| Bug | Hit in | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| **`forwardRef(...) as X` cast unwrapping** — none of our 3 forwardRef detectors unwrap a trailing `as` cast | Fluent UI (cast on the `forwardRef` call itself) **and** Ark UI (same pattern, independently) — 2 of 4 libraries, unrelated codebases | 🔴 Highest ROI — one fix, two real-world hits |
| **Same-file TS `namespace X { type Props }` resolution** — stored under bare name (`"Props"`), looked up under dotted name (`"X.Props"`) | Base UI — MenuRoot degrades to empty props w/ diagnostic; MenuTrigger is fully invisible with **zero diagnostics** (worse — silent, not even degraded) | 🔴 High — silent failure with no error trail |
| **`@deprecated` JSDoc bleeds onto unrelated sibling props** | Ant Design — `iconPosition`'s tag leaks onto `iconPlacement`, `shape`, `size`, `disabled` | 🟡 Medium — likely same root cause as the description-leak bug we already fixed once, recurring at prop level |
| **Generic type alias substitution** (`Assign<T,U>`-style user-defined generics) — `T`/`U` leak as literal unresolved names instead of substituting | Ark UI's original `SelectRootProps<T> = Assign<HTMLProps<'div'>, SelectRootBaseProps<T>>` | 🟠 Structurally bigger — worth its own scoped investigation before committing to an approach, same way the HTML-attributes spike turned out easier than feared |

One nuance worth flagging before you decide next steps: **the Fluent UI and Base UI fixtures currently sit "red"** (they still contain the real bug-triggering pattern verbatim and extract 0 components today) — good, honest regression tests once fixed. But **the Ant Design and Ark UI fixtures had to be rewritten away from the exact patterns that broke them** just to produce any comparable output at all, so as committed they no longer regression-test bugs #1 (Ark's forwardRef-cast) or #4 (Ark's generic substitution) — only bug #3 (AntD's JSDoc bleed) still reproduces in its fixture.

Good progress — the investigation confirms the hypothesis and already has a passing fix. Here's the status:

**Verdict: confirmed tractable, no type inference needed.** Pure structural substitution handles it.

**Root causes found** — two independent gaps, not one:
1. Type alias declarations never recorded their own parameter names (`T`, `U`) at all — the extractor ignored `node.type_parameters` entirely, and call-site type arguments were computed but discarded before ever reaching alias resolution.

## Round 2: 5 findings, 2 are real competitive gaps vs RDT

| # | Library | Finding | Vs RDT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Blueprint Table** | Interface extending *two* different `Partial<X>` mixins silently drops the second one's fields (`defaultColumnWidth`, `maxColumnWidth`, `minColumnWidth`) — zero diagnostic, violates the project's own "never fail silently" rule | **We're behind**: 45 vs RDT's 48 props |
| 2 | **Day Picker** | Discriminant detection only fires when a type alias's RHS is *directly* a union (`type X = A\|B`) — when wrapped in an intersection (`Base & (A\|B\|C...)`, a very common real pattern), it falls into a naive first-branch-wins merge. `discriminantProp` comes back `null`, and `selected`'s type collapses to just `Date` instead of the real `Date \| Date[] \| DateRange` | **We're behind**: RDT gets the full union right, we don't |
| 3 | **Headless UI** | `forwardRefWithAs(NamedFn)`-style identifier indirection (the render function is a separately-declared top-level function, not inline) produces a *spurious, wrongly-named* component (`ButtonFn` instead of the real export `ListboxButton`) | Mixed — RDT gets the name right but explodes `PropsOf<TTag>` to 234–246 props from every possible HTML element and collapses `onChange` to `any` |
| 4 | Day Picker (secondary) | Bare function-type aliases (`type Handler<T> = (...) => void`) aren't classified at all, causing spurious "cannot resolve" warnings | Minor, unrelated to the union bug |
| 5 | Zendesk Garden | `styled.button.attrs<T>()` isn't recognized as a component-defining pattern at all | **Shared blind spot** — RDT misses this too (and produces a spurious false-positive elsewhere), so not a competitive gap |

Findings #1 and #2 are the strongest candidates — both are confirmed, well-isolated (Blueprint's agent already has a 10-line minimal repro), common real-world patterns, and genuine regressions relative to RDT rather than shared limitations. #3 is real but murkier (both tools have issues, just different ones) and #5 doesn't hurt us competitively.

Adds the pipeline-side half of Full mode: resolves @types/react's real
.d.ts path (reusing the resolver's oxc_resolver-based specifier
resolution, now exposed as resolve_package_dts_path), parses it through
the same DTS cache as any other .d.ts, and merges it into
GlobalSourceData before resolution runs — so ButtonHTMLAttributes,
HTMLAttributes, etc. are real, lookupable interfaces instead of only
ever being collapsed to InheritedLayer metadata. Emits a diagnostic
(never fails silently) if @types/react can't be resolved at all, falling
back to curated behavior.

Also fixes the interface lookup key in extends.rs: @types/react declares
everything inside `declare namespace React { ... }`, so once merged
these interfaces are stored under the namespace-qualified key
(React.ButtonHTMLAttributes) by the earlier namespace-qualification fix —
the lookup was stripping "React." instead of using it, so it always
missed. Now tries the qualified key first, falling back to bare for
resilience.

Verified end-to-end against this repo's real, installed @types/react
(not synthetic test data): a real Button component extending
React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> resolves 235 real props.

Known follow-up, not fixed here: a handful of fields inside
@types/react's own interface chain (AriaAttributes referenced bare from
within the same enclosing namespace, not through an explicit React.
qualifier) don't resolve — same-namespace sibling reference resolution
is narrower than qualified-reference resolution. Degrades gracefully
(a diagnostic, not a crash); doesn't block the feature.
EOF
)"

1	# Migrating from react-docgen-typescript
2	
3	`oxc-react-docgen` targets output-shape compatibility with `react-docgen-typescript` (RDT) via the CLI's `--format rdt` flag. The NAPI binding and Vite plugin currently only expose the tool's own canonical format (`kind`-tagged `PropType`, shown in the main README) — there's no RDT-shape option at that layer yet. This document covers what's compatible today, what's intentionally different, and what's a known gap rather than a design choice.
4	
5	**Should you switch today?** If your components use plain interfaces/type aliases, `forwardRef`, `FC`, HOC wrapping, `Omit`/`Pick`, or `VariantProps` (CVA/TV/PandaCSS) — yes, output should match closely. If you scrape the full 250+ inherited HTML attributes per component, or rely on deeply nested discriminated unions, read the [HTML attribute inheritance](#html-attribute-inheritance) and [Known bugs](#known-bugs-not-design-choices) sections below first.
6	
7	## Field-by-field comparison
8	
9	### Component level (`ComponentDoc`)
10	
11	| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| `displayName` | ✅ | |
14	| `description` | ✅ | From the component's own leading JSDoc, if any |
15	| `props` | ✅ | See prop-level table below |
16	| `methods` | ✅ (always `[]`) | RDT only populates this for class components; we don't support class components, so it's always empty — present for shape compatibility, not because we detect methods |
17	| `tags` | ✅ | JSDoc `@tag` values on the component declaration (e.g. `@deprecated`, `@since`) — not part of RDT's original spec but included since some tooling reads it |
18	
19	### Prop level (`PropItem`)
20	
21	| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `name` | ✅ | |
24	| `required` | ✅ | |
25	| `type.name` | ✅ | Literal unions emit `{name: "enum", value: [...]}` matching RDT's convention (so Storybook-style `<select>` controls activate) instead of inlining the literal text |
26	| `description` | ✅ | |
27	| `defaultValue` | ✅ | `{value, computed}` — captured from destructured parameter defaults (`{ variant = 'primary' }`) or JSDoc `@default`, code value wins on conflict |
28	| `parent.name` / `parent.fileName` | ✅ | `fileName` is always canonicalized to an absolute path regardless of how `--src` was invoked |
29	| `declarations` | ❌ not emitted in `--format rdt` | Only present in `--format canonical` (the raw internal shape); omitted from both `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` to match RDT's single-parent shape. File an issue if you need it |
30	
31	### Intentionally omitted
32	
33	| Prop | Why |
34	|---|---|
35	| `ref` | Not a user-facing prop — a React internal. RDT includes it because it walks the full inherited type; we treat it as noise |
36	| `key` | Same reasoning as `ref` |
37	
38	### HTML attribute inheritance
39	
40	RDT inlines every inherited HTML attribute (e.g. all ~250-300 members of `ButtonHTMLAttributes`) directly into `props`. We don't — instead:
41	
42	- `inheritance` (canonical format only) records the layer itself (`ButtonHTMLAttributes`, the element it maps to, what was `Omit`-ted).
43	- `notableInherited` surfaces ~15-20 curated, commonly-documented HTML attributes per element (`onClick`, `disabled`, `type`, ARIA attributes, etc.) rather than the full set.
44	- `--format rdt` does **not** include `notableInherited` at all — RDT consumers that filter by `parent.fileName.includes('node_modules')` to drop inherited noise will simply see fewer inherited props than RDT provides, not extra/wrong ones.
45	
46	If your tooling depends on the full inherited-attribute list being present, this is the biggest real compatibility gap — not a bug, but a deliberate scope decision to keep output focused on what a component actually documents.
47

This document covers what's compatible today, what's intentionally different, and what's a known gap rather than a design choice.
4	
5	**Should you switch today?** If your components use plain interfaces/type aliases, `forwardRef` (including wrapped in an `as` cast), `FC`, HOC wrapping, `Omit`/`Pick`, `VariantProps` (CVA/TV/PandaCSS), or discriminated unions (including ones wrapped in an intersection) — yes, output should match closely. If you scrape the full 250+ inherited HTML attributes per component, read the [HTML attribute inheritance](#html-attribute-inheritance) section below — it's supported, but opt-in.

8	
9	### Component level (`ComponentDoc`)
10	
11	| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| `displayName` | ✅ | |
14	| `description` | ✅ | From the component's own leading JSDoc, if any |
15	| `props` | ✅ | See prop-level table below |
16	| `methods` | ✅ (always `[]`) | RDT only populates this for class components; we don't support class components, so it's always empty — present for shape compatibility, not because we detect methods |
17	| `tags` | ✅ | JSDoc `@tag` values on the component declaration (e.g. `@deprecated`, `@since`) — not part of RDT's original spec but included since some tooling reads it |
18	
19	### Prop level (`PropItem`)
20	
21	| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `name` | ✅ | |
24	| `required` | ✅ | |
25	| `type.name` | ✅ | Literal unions emit `{name: "enum", value: [...]}` matching RDT's convention (so Storybook-style `<select>` controls activate) instead of inlining the literal text |
26	| `description` | ✅ | |
27	| `defaultValue` | ✅ | `{value, computed}` — captured from destructured parameter defaults (`{ variant = 'primary' }`) or JSDoc `@default`, code value wins on conflict |
28	| `parent.name` / `parent.fileName` | ✅ | `fileName` is always canonicalized to an absolute path regardless of how `--src` was invoked |
29	| `declarations` | ❌ not emitted in `--format rdt` | Only present in `--format canonical` (the raw internal shape); omitted from both `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` to match RDT's single-parent shape. File an issue if you need it |

32	
33	| Prop | Why |
34	|---|---|
35	| `ref` | Not a user-facing prop — a React internal. RDT includes it because it walks the full inherited type; we treat it as noise |
36	| `key` | Same reasoning as `ref` |

39	
40	RDT inlines every inherited HTML attribute (e.g. all ~250-300 members of `ButtonHTMLAttributes`) directly into `props`. By default, we don't — but you can turn this on:
41

1	# oxc-react-docgen
2	
3	React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax.
4	
5	> **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, and CLI are complete. Config file loading is the next milestone.
6	
7	## Why
8	
9	`react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system this takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass, so cold extraction on a 15-component fixture set (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, Radix) takes **32ms**.
10	
11	The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet.
12	
13	## Install
14	
15	`@oxc-react-docgen/napi`, `@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin`, and `@oxc-react-docgen/cli` are not yet published to npm — there are no per-platform prebuilt binaries to install today. Until a release ships:
16	
17	```bash
18	git clone https://github.com/castrog/oxc-react-codegen
19	cd oxc-react-codegen
20	pnpm install
21	pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi run build:napi   # builds the native addon for your platform
22	pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
23	```
24	
25	`pnpm run build:napi` (not a bare `cargo build`) matters: it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s generated loader expects it. This works as a monorepo-local dependency today; there are no published per-platform packages for it to fall back to yet. See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) if you're moving off `react-docgen-typescript` and want to know exactly what's compatible today.
26	
27	## Vite plugin
28	
29	```ts
30	// vite.config.ts
31	import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
32	import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
33	import { oxcReactDocgen } from '@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin'
34	
35	export default defineConfig({
36	  plugins: [
37	    react(),
38	    oxcReactDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] }),
39	  ],
40	})
41	```
42	
43	Metadata is available on the `virtual:oxc-react-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change:
44	
45	```ts
46	import docgen from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'
47	
48	docgen.components['Button'].props
49	// {
50	//   variant: {
51	//     type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true },
52	//     required: false,
53	//     defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false },
54	//     description: '',
55	//   },
56	//   ...
57	// }
58	```
59	
60	## CLI
61	
62	The CLI is a single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and
63	`--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there and nowhere else.
64	`@oxc-react-docgen/cli` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that just execs the
65	platform-appropriate compiled binary; it deliberately contains no reimplementation of CLI
66	behavior, so there's exactly one place that behavior can drift.
67	
68	```bash
69	# Once published: npx @oxc-react-docgen/cli extract --src src/ --out docgen.json
70	# From source today: ./target/release/oxc-react-docgen (after cargo build --release)
71	
72	# One-shot extraction
73	oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json
74	
75	# Inspect a single file
76	oxc-react-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx
77	
78	# Watch mode
79	oxc-react-docgen watch --src src/
80	
81	# Shell completions
82	oxc-react-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_oxc-react-docgen
83	```

export type ReactTag = keyof React.JSX.IntrinsicElements | React.JSXElementConstructor<any>

export type Expand<T> = T extends infer O ? { [K in keyof O]: O[K] } : never

export type PropsOf<TTag extends ReactTag> = TTag extends React.ElementType
  ? Omit<React.ComponentProps<TTag>, 'ref'>
  : never

type PropsWeControl = 'as' | 'children' | 'refName' | 'className'

// Resolve the props of the component, but ensure to omit certain props that we control
type CleanProps<TTag extends ReactTag, TOmittableProps extends PropertyKey = never> = Omit<
  PropsOf<TTag>,
  TOmittableProps | PropsWeControl
>

// Add certain props that we control
type OurProps<TTag extends ReactTag, TSlot> = {
  as?: TTag
  children?: React.ReactNode | ((bag: TSlot) => React.ReactElement)
  refName?: string
}

type HasProperty<T extends object, K extends PropertyKey> = T extends never
  ? never
  : K extends keyof T
    ? true
    : never

// Conditionally override the `className`, to also allow for a function
// if and only if the PropsOf<TTag> already defines `className`.
// This will allow us to have a TS error on as={Fragment}
type ClassNameOverride<TTag extends ReactTag, TSlot = {}> =
  // Order is important here, because `never extends true` is `true`...
  true extends HasProperty<PropsOf<TTag>, 'className'>
    ? { className?: PropsOf<TTag>['className'] | ((bag: TSlot) => string) }
    : {}

// Provide clean TypeScript props, which exposes some of our custom APIs.
export type Props<
  TTag extends ReactTag,
  TSlot = {},
  TOmittableProps extends PropertyKey = never,
  Overrides = {},
> = CleanProps<TTag, TOmittableProps | keyof Overrides> &
  OurProps<TTag, TSlot> &
  ClassNameOverride<TTag, TSlot> &
  Overrides

export type EnsureArray<T> = T extends any[] ? T : Expand<T>[]

## Q1 — Is `extra_builtins` user-configurable from the CLI/config today?

**No.** The full chain:

- `crates/core/src/react_types.rs:35` — `is_react_builtin(name, extra: &FxHashSet<CompactString>)`, comment at line 34: *"extra allows callers... to pass additional builtin names from PipelineOptions.extra_builtins without needing to change this file."*
- `crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs:53` — `ResolutionContext.extra_builtins: FxHashSet<CompactString>`; populated at `crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs:89` inside `ResolutionContext::new`: `extra_builtins: options.extra_builtins.clone()`.
- `crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs:80` — `PipelineOptions.extra_builtins: FxHashSet<compact_str::CompactString>` (doc: "Additional builtin type names beyond the React standard set"). Defaults to `Default::default()` (empty) at `crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs:103`.
- **NAPI binding** (`crates/binding/src/lib.rs`): `JsExtractOptions.extra_builtins: Option<Vec<String>>` (line 41), converted into the `FxHashSet<CompactString>` at lines 58-59 and threaded into `PipelineOptions` at line 98. This is a real, working programmatic entry point.
- **CLI**: `crates/cli/src/main.rs` — `ExtractArgs` (lines 62-91) has no `--extra-builtins`/equivalent flag at all.
- **Config file**: `crates/cli/src/config.rs:7-9` — the doc comment on `DocgenConfigSchema` explicitly says it's *"a deliberate subset of PipelineOptions — everything except the fields that need complex map/object values (extraPaths, knownTypeOverrides, extraBuiltins), which aren't supported via config file yet."* The struct (lines 14-26) has no `extra_builtins` field, and `deny_unknown_fields` (line 13) means a user who adds `extraBuiltins` to `docgen.config.ts` gets a hard error, not silent ignoring. `into_pipeline_options()` (lines 30-72) never sets `opts.extra_builtins`, so it stays the empty default from `PipelineOptions::default()`.

**Conclusion:** `extra_builtins` is currently settable only via the Rust API (`PipelineOptions` struct literal) or the NAPI/JS binding (`JsExtractOptions.extra_builtins`). A CLI user has **no way** to add a custom name without recompiling — neither a flag nor a config-file field exists, and the config schema explicitly documents this as a known gap.

## Q2 — Any TS-lib (`lib.es5.d.ts`/`lib.dom.d.ts`) parsing infrastructure?

**No — purely react-specific today.** The `HtmlAttributeMode::Full` logic in `crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs:285-330` (Phase 3.5) hardcodes `"react"` as the package name: `crate::resolver::resolve_package_dts_path(&from_dir, "react")` (line 305), then reads/parses/caches that one file and merges it via `global.merge(&react_dts_path, data)` (line 313). `resolve_package_dts_path` (`crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs:101-110`) and `resolve_package_types_file` (`crates/core/src/resolver/react.rs:129-...`) are both generic-looking (take `package_name: &str`) but are only ever invoked with `"react"` (`crates/core/src/resolver/react.rs:119`) or `"@types/react"` in tests (`crates/core/src/resolver/react.rs:252`). Nothing in the codebase calls them with `"typescript"` or references `lib.es5`/`lib.dom`/ambient/`EcmaGlobal` — a repo-wide grep for those terms turned up zero hits outside this analysis. Instead, natively-global types like `Date` fall through to `named.rs`'s step-6 hardcoded allowlist or step-7's diagnostic (see below) — there's no ambient-global resolution path at all.

**`typescript` package presence:** No top-level `node_modules/typescript` (pnpm doesn't hoist it there; `ls` confirms `node_modules/typescript` doesn't exist). It is present transitively in pnpm's content-addressed store at `node_modules/.pnpm/typescript@5.9.3/node_modules/typescript/lib/`, which does contain `lib.es5.d.ts` (213K) and `lib.dom.d.ts` (1.8M), confirmed via `ls -la`. It is not a direct dependency in the root `package.json` (no `"typescript"` line found there). So the files exist and are reachable, but not at a predictable un-versioned path the way `resolve_package_dts_path` currently expects for npm packages — using it would require pnpm-store-aware resolution.

## Q3 — How diagnostics reach the CLI user

`ExtractionOutput.diagnostics` flows to `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:33` (`output = pipeline::extract(&options)`), then, only when `!json_mode && !quiet`, to `print_summary(&output, quiet)` and `print_diagnostics(&output.diagnostics)` (lines 44-47). In `--json` mode, the function returns early at line 41 after printing the raw serialized `output` (diagnostics included as plain JSON array) — no human-readable diagnostic text at all in that mode.

**No `miette` involvement for diagnostics.** `Diagnostic` (`crates/core/src/types/diagnostic.rs:6-15`) has no `miette::Diagnostic` derive/impl anywhere in the repo (confirmed via grep) — `miette` is used only for command-level `Result<()>`/error propagation (`IntoDiagnostic`, `WrapErr` in `extract.rs:1`), contradicting the CLAUDE.md aspiration that "error display uses miette" for diagnostics specifically.

Actual display, in `crates/cli/src/output.rs`:
- `print_summary` (lines 4-32): one-line colored summary to **stderr** — component/enum counts, `"{warnings} warnings"` and `"{errors} errors"` counts (yellow/red via `owo_colors` if nonzero), duration.
- `print_diagnostics` (lines 35-53): flat list to stderr, one line per diagnostic: `  [{prefix}] {file}:{message}` (or without file), plus an indented `help:` line if present. `prefix` is `"error"` (red), `"warn"` (yellow), or `"info"` (dimmed) per severity (lines 38-43).

No grouping by file, no per-code distinction, no summary breakdown by `DiagnosticCode`, and severities are not gated by `--verbose`/`-v` — `verbose` only controls `init_tracing` log level (`main.rs:167-172`), unrelated to diagnostic visibility. The only visibility switch is `--quiet` (suppresses both) and `--json` (suppresses the human-readable path entirely, diagnostics only appear inside the JSON blob). `extract.rs:60-63` additionally makes the process `exit(2)` if any diagnostic has `Error` severity — `Warning`-severity items like `UnresolvableImport` never affect exit code.</result>

Good instincts on both counts — and digging into `DependencyList` specifically turned up something more interesting than a missing allowlist entry.

**1. Native JS globals (`Date`, etc.)** — you're right that these shouldn't need special-casing at all in principle. Two real options:
- **Allowlist (quick):** add `Date` and a handful of common ES/DOM globals (`RegExp`, `Map`, `Set`, `Element`, `Node`, etc.) to the same silent list `Promise`/`Symbol`/`BigInt` already live in. One line each, zero risk, but perpetual whack-a-mole — every native global a user's code touches that we haven't seen yet is a future diagnostic.
- **Parse TypeScript's own lib files (principled, bigger):** `lib.es5.d.ts`/`lib.dom.d.ts` genuinely exist in `node_modules/.pnpm/typescript@.../lib/` and declare every one of these ambient-globally, so in theory we could resolve `Date` the same real way we resolve `@types/react`. But `typescript` isn't a direct dependency here, the file is 1.8MB (`lib.dom.d.ts` alone), and ambient `declare global` shapes are a different parsing case than anything we handle today. That's a real feature, not a quick fix.

My take: do the allowlist now, leave lib-file parsing as a "maybe later if this keeps recurring."

**2. `DependencyList` — you were right to push on this, and it's not just an allowlist question.** It's declared as `import * as React from "react"` + `React.DependencyList` — a **namespace import**, not a named one. I checked, and it fails to resolve even in `--html-attributes full` mode, where `@types/react` genuinely is parsed and the type genuinely is there. The actual bug: `resolve_to_canonical` only strips the `"React."` prefix for the *builtin-name check* — it never treats `React` as an alias for the `"react"` package when routing a `React.X` member access through import resolution, so it always falls back to a same-file lookup instead of using the `import * as React` binding at all. That's a real, scoped bug in the same family as last round's fixes, and fixing it would resolve `DependencyList` — and any other `React.X`-via-namespace-import reference — through the normal mechanism, no allowlist entry needed. This is the better fix, and it's the kind of thing I should just do rather than paper over with a hardcoded name.

**3. Diagnostic UX — agreed, and today it's worse than it needs to be.** Right now every occurrence prints its own line (`[warn] file:message`), so `Date` alone would be 101 near-identical lines. There's no grouping by type name, no distinction between severities beyond a color prefix, and it's stderr-only in JSON mode (buried in the output blob, no human-readable path at all). Worth fixing: dedupe by `(code, type name)` with an occurrence count — turns 101 lines into one.

**4. One more thing the research surfaced, relevant to "configurable":** the `extra_builtins` allowlist-extension mechanism already exists in `PipelineOptions`/the NAPI binding, but there's **no CLI flag or `docgen.config.ts` field for it** — the config schema's own doc comment admits this ("aren't supported via config file yet"). So right now a CLI user genuinely can't extend the list without recompiling.

Given all that, here's what I'd propose, roughly in priority order: (1) fix the `React.X` namespace-import resolution bug — real bug, general benefit; (2) expand the native-JS-globals allowlist; (3) expose `extra_builtins` via a CLI flag + config field so users aren't stuck waiting on us for every future name; (4) dedupe diagnostic output by type name. Switching to `usize` with `saturating_sub` makes the invalid state *unrepresentable* rather than just guarded against — the preferred fix whenever you can afford it, since a representable-but-invalid intermediate value is exactly the kind of thing that bites you two features later, in a file you'll never think to test.

# Migrating from react-docgen-typescript

`oxc-react-docgen` targets output-shape compatibility with `react-docgen-typescript` (RDT) via the CLI's `--format rdt` flag. The NAPI binding and Vite plugin currently only expose the tool's own canonical format (`kind`-tagged `PropType`, shown in the main README) — there's no RDT-shape option at that layer yet. This document covers what's compatible today, what's intentionally different, and what's a known gap rather than a design choice.

**Should you switch today?** If your components use plain interfaces/type aliases, `forwardRef` (including wrapped in an `as` cast), `FC`, HOC wrapping, `Omit`/`Pick`, `VariantProps` (CVA/TV/PandaCSS), or discriminated unions (including ones wrapped in an intersection) — yes, output should match closely. If you scrape the full 250+ inherited HTML attributes per component, read the [HTML attribute inheritance](#html-attribute-inheritance) section below — it's supported, but opt-in.

# oxc-react-docgen

React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax.

> **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete.

## Why

`react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system this takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass, so cold extraction on a 15-component fixture set (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, Radix) takes **32ms**.

The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet.

## Install

`@oxc-react-docgen/napi`, `@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin`, and `@oxc-react-docgen/cli` are not yet published to npm — there are no per-platform prebuilt binaries to install today. Until a release ships:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/castrog/oxc-react-codegen
cd oxc-react-codegen
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi run build:napi   # builds the native addon for your platform
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
```

`pnpm run build:napi` (not a bare `cargo build`) matters: it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s generated loader expects it. This works as a monorepo-local dependency today; there are no published per-platform packages for it to fall back to yet. See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) if you're moving off `react-docgen-typescript` and want to know exactly what's compatible today.

## Vite plugin

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { oxcReactDocgen } from '@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    oxcReactDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] }),
  ],
})
```

Metadata is available on the `virtual:oxc-react-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change:

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
// {
//   variant: {
//     type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true },
//     required: false,
//     defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false },
//     description: '',
//   },
//   ...
// }
```

## CLI

The CLI is a single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and
`--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there and nowhere else.
`@oxc-react-docgen/cli` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that just execs the
platform-appropriate compiled binary; it deliberately contains no reimplementation of CLI
behavior, so there's exactly one place that behavior can drift.

```bash
# Once published: npx @oxc-react-docgen/cli extract --src src/ --out docgen.json
# From source today: ./target/release/oxc-react-docgen (after cargo build --release)

# One-shot extraction
oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json

# Inspect a single file
oxc-react-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx

# Watch mode
oxc-react-docgen watch --src src/

# Shell completions
oxc-react-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_oxc-react-docgen

# Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset
oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full
```

Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and
more — see `crates/cli/src/config.rs` for the full schema) instead of CLI flags.

# Architecture

## Pipeline

Every extraction — cold or incremental — flows through four phases:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    src["Source files\n.ts / .tsx / .d.ts"]
    oxc["OXC parser\none allocator per file"]
    sd["SourceData\ninterfaces, type aliases,\nimport bindings, defaults"]
    gsd["GlobalSourceData\nmerged across all files\nArc<ArcSwap<…>>"]
    ce["ComponentEntry\nresolved props,\ninheritance chain"]
    out["ExtractionOutput\nJSON-serializable"]

    src -->|"discover_files()\nignore crate"| oxc
    oxc -->|"parse_file()\nper-file parallel"| sd
    sd -->|"rayon par_iter\nmerge()"| gsd
    gsd -->|"resolve_component()\nper-component parallel"| ce
    ce -->|"pipeline::extract()"| out
```

Each `parse_file()` call gets its own OXC allocator. No AST node escapes the function — all extracted data is owned, heap-allocated types. This is what makes the rayon parallelism safe.

The watch path reuses `GlobalSourceData` across file changes. A single-file update calls `parse_file()` on the changed file, merges via `ArcSwap::rcu` (retries on concurrent write), then re-resolves only the affected components.

## Crate and package graph

```mermaid
graph TD
    core["crates/core\noxc-react-docgen-core\nPure extraction — no I/O, no async"]
    binding["crates/binding\noxc-react-docgen-napi\nNAPI + tokio runtime"]
    cli["crates/cli\noxc-react-docgen\nCLI binary"]
    napi["packages/napi\n@oxc-react-docgen/napi\nTS types + dev binary loader"]
    vite["packages/vite-plugin\n@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin\nVite HMR plugin"]
    validate["apps/validate\nAccuracy comparison harness"]

    core --> binding
    core --> cli
    binding --> napi
    napi --> vite
    cli -.->|"runtime dep"| validate
    napi -.->|"runtime dep"| validate
```

`crates/core` has no dependency on async runtimes, NAPI, or terminal libraries. It can be linked from any host.

# Contributing

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Min version | Notes |
|------|------------|-------|
| Rust | 1.94 | `rustup update stable` |
| proto | latest | manages Node/pnpm versions from `.prototools` |
| pnpm | 9 | via proto, or `npm i -g pnpm` |

After installing proto, run `moon setup` once to pull the pinned Node version and any other tool versions declared in `.prototools`.

## Build & test

```bash
# Rust
cargo build                                            # dev build
cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core                   # 100 unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p oxc-react-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all

# TypeScript
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test      # 14 vitest tests

# Accuracy comparison (informational — exits 0 regardless of gaps)
moon run validate:compare
```

The pre-commit hook runs `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `typos`, and `cargo deny` on every commit. If you're on a machine where the hook fires on every `git commit`, the hook is fast enough that it's not worth bypassing.

## Snapshot tests

Snapshot tests use [insta](https://insta.rs). Each fixture (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, etc.) has a snapshot of the full extraction output. If your change touches extraction output, insta will flag it:

```bash
cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core    # fails with "snapshot mismatch"
cargo insta review                     # review diffs, accept or reject
```

Accept any snapshot change that is intentional (i.e., the output got more accurate). Reject regressions.

## Where code goes

**`crates/core`** — everything that understands TypeScript ASTs and React component patterns. No I/O, no async, no terminal output. Every function here must be `Send + Sync` so rayon can parallelize it.

**`crates/cli`** — user-facing output only. No extraction logic. Commands parse args and delegate to `core::pipeline`. Error formatting uses `miette`; progress uses `indicatif`; table output uses `comfy-table`.

**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the five NAPI functions (`extractAll`, `createSession`, `initializeSession`, `extractFileIncremental`, `closeSession`). No business logic.

**`packages/napi`** — `@oxc-react-docgen/napi`. TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`) and the dev binary loader (`index.js`) that finds the `.node` file from `target/` or `NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH`. No logic.

**`packages/vite-plugin`** — `@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin`. Single Vite `Plugin` object. No extraction logic — calls NAPI and manages HMR.

## Code style

The authoritative reference is `.claude/skills/rust-style/SKILL.md`. Highlights:

**Maps:** `FxHashMap` for internal maps (hot path, no DoS surface). `BTreeMap` for anything that ends up in JSON output (key ordering must be deterministic and stable across runs).

**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.

**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
```

**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.

**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.

**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.

## Commits

- GPG-signed, `Signed-off-by` trailer (both configured in `.git/config`)
- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix
- No line wrapping at any column
- Subject line says it all — skip the body if it adds nothing

```
# good
feat: resolve ComponentPropsWithoutRef in intersection type aliases

Updated the resolver to also handle the case where ComponentPropsWithoutRef
appears inside an intersection type a...

## Validation Strategy

We compare output against two baselines on the same fixture files:

| Tool | Basis | What it proves |
|------|-------|----------------|
| `react-docgen` 7.x | babel, JS/TSX only | detection accuracy vs the original |
| `react-docgen-typescript` 2.x | tsc, full type resolution | the primary drop-in target |
| **ours** | OXC, no tsc | speed + correctness |

Infrastructure: `packages/validate/` — run `pnpm baseline` then `pnpm compare`.

### Validation fixture libraries (priority order)

1. **shadcn/ui** — cva + forwardRef + VariantProps ✅ in fixtures
2. **Radix UI** — ComponentPropsWithoutRef + asChild ✅ in fixtures
3. **MUI** — deepest type chains, SxProps, OverridableStringUnion ✅ in fixtures
4. **Chakra UI** — HTMLChakraProps, ThemingProps ✅ in fixtures
5. **Mantine** — StylesApiProps, polymorphic component ✅ in fixtures
6. **React Aria** — ARIA-first, render props, no HTML inheritance ✅ in fixtures

### Accuracy dimensions to validate

- Components detected (false positives, false negatives)
- Prop names (completeness)
- Type accuracy (`"string" | "number"` vs `"enum"`)
- Required/optional correctness
- Default values extracted
- JSDoc descriptions preserved
- `parent.fileName` pointing to correct file (critical for RDT propFilter compat)
- Speed: our tool vs rdt (target: 10-100x faster)

## React Best Practices — Implementation Gaps

### React 19 `ref` as plain prop
In React 19, `ref` is passed as a regular prop — `forwardRef` is no longer
needed and is deprecated. The extractor must detect:
```tsx
// React 19 — ref is just a prop
function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps & { ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }) {}
```
`ReactVersion.ref_as_prop` exists in `react_types.rs` — Phase 2a must wire it up.

### Compound components
`Dialog.Trigger`, `Select.Item` etc. are not addressed in Phase 2a spec.
Pattern: `const DialogTrigger = Dialog.Trigger` or `Dialog.Trigger = DialogTrigger`.
Decision needed: detect and emit as separate components, or skip?
**Recommendation:** emit as `Dialog.Trigger` display name, separate ComponentEntry.

### `displayName` fallback
Some HOC-wrapped components set `Comp.displayName = 'Button'` after definition.
Phase 2a extractor must scan for `MemberExpression.displayName = StringLiteral`
assignments to correct the component name.

### `defaultProps` (deprecated but present in .d.ts)
MUI ships `defaultProps` in its .d.ts declarations. We should read them as
default values rather than ignoring them. Phase 3a resolver decision.

### Generic components
`Table<TData extends object>`, `Select<T>` etc. — the extractor currently
only handles non-generic component patterns. Phase 2a: when a component's
props type has type params, emit `Named { name, args }` and let the resolver
degrade gracefully.

## Note: slot recipes — partial support

`defineSlotRecipe` (PandaCSS) and `tv({ slots })` (tailwind-variants) are in the recognized callee list and benefit from the 2026-06-28 arg-index fix. However, slot recipe variant values are objects (`{ root: "class", header: "class" }`) rather than plain strings. The current `try_collect_cva_call` variant value extraction reads only string values, so slot recipe variants will have 0 entries in `global.enums` even after the arg-index fix.

The `RecipeVariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>` reference will fall back to opaque output with `raw: "VariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>"` in the `composes` array. This is documented as a limitation, not a bug.

Found a real bug — pre-existing, not something this session's changes introduced, but the sweep caught it.

antd's actual `Button` export chain is:
```ts
const InternalCompoundedButton = React.forwardRef<...>((props, ref) => {...});
const Button = InternalCompoundedButton;        // plain identifier alias
Button.displayName = 'Button';                   // then a displayName assignment on the alias
export default Button;
```

`try_scan_display_name` looks for a `ComponentMapping` whose name matches the assignment's left side (`"Button"`) — but the actual detected mapping is still named `InternalCompoundedButton`, because `const Button = InternalCompoundedButton;` (a bare identifier alias, not a `forwardRef`/`memo`/HOC call) doesn't trigger any of the existing component-detection or renaming paths. The props extraction itself is fine — the component just surfaces under the wrong name (`InternalCompoundedButton` instead of `Button`), which is exactly what a real consumer would see for antd's actual flagship component.

Fixing this properly: detect `const NewName = ExistingIdentifier;` where `ExistingIdentifier` matches an already-detected `ComponentMapping`, and rename the mapping — the same shape as the existing "identifier-wrapped component renamed to export binding" fix from earlier this session, just without a wrapping call in between. Adversarial review found two related correctness bugs in how static
property assignments (displayName, defaultProps) and identifier
aliases rename/find ComponentMapping entries:

1. try_scan_display_name renamed mapping.component_name to the
   *string value* of `X.displayName = "..."` immediately. When that
   string differs from the variable identifier (a real pattern — an
   internal implementation name exposed under a nicer public
   displayName), a later `X.defaultProps = {...}` referencing the
   *original* identifier could no longer find the mapping. Fixed by
   deferring the rename: try_scan_display_name now records the pending
   rename on the collector and finish() applies it as the very last
   step, after every other scan has already had its chance to look
   mappings up by their original identifier for the whole file.

2. try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component renamed the matched mapping
   in place. A second, different alias to the same base
   (`const A = Base; const Bcopy = Base;`) could never find the base
   again — the first alias had already renamed it away — silently
   dropping the second alias with no trace. Fixed by cloning the
   matched mapping under the new name instead of mutating it, with the
   base's own (implementation-only) name filtered out of the final
   output in finish() via a new aliased_away set.

Also extracted two shared helpers this touched anyway: static_member_
assignment (X.Y = <expr> parsing, shared by try_scan_display_name and
try_scan_default_props — they were previously identical end to end)

prologue shared by try_collect_const_enum and try_collect_const_array).

fixtures) still pass unchanged — these were real but previously
untested edge cases, not regressions in already-covered behavior.

fix(pipeline): fix watch-mode's real correctness and perf gaps

Adversarial review found watch mode wasn't actually correct or
incremental in four compounding ways:

1. WatchSession::initialize() rebuilt GlobalSourceData by hand
   (discover -> parse -> merge only), skipping Phase 3.5 (@types/react
   Full-mode merge) and Phase 3.6 (ambient lib.d.ts merge, this
   session's own earlier feature) entirely. The cold `output` it
   returned was correct (built via a real extract() call done
   separately just for that output), but self.global — what every
   subsequent update_file() resolves against — was not. Fixed by
   factoring extract() into extract_with_global(), a single real
   pipeline run shared by both the one-shot and watch-mode paths, so
   there's exactly one implementation to keep in sync going forward.

2. ReverseDeps::build was never called — reverse_deps stayed
   permanently empty, so update_file's BFS dependent-propagation only
   ever found the changed file itself, never files that import it.
   Fixed by computing it in initialize() from the now-correctly-merged
   global (required changing the field from Arc<ReverseDeps> to
   ArcSwap<ReverseDeps> so initialize() can populate it with &self).

3. Found while writing a real-tempdir test for #2: update_file's
   `changed` path isn't canonicalized, but discover_files' walker (via
   the `ignore` crate) resolves symlinks in the paths it reports (e.g.
   macOS's /var -> /private/var) — so a file-watcher-reported path
   would never match reverse_deps'/global's keys unless canonicalized
   the same way, silently finding no dependents regardless of #2's
   fix. Added canonicalize_best_effort (falls back to canonicalizing
   the parent dir when the full path doesn't resolve yet, so a file's
   key stays stable across its own create/delete transitions).

4. resolve_ts_lib_paths re-ran a fresh oxc_resolver filesystem walk on
   every ResolutionContext::new — i.e. every single update_file call —
   even though its result (options.src_dirs never changes within a
   session) can't change between saves. Added
   ResolutionContext::new_with_cached_ambient_global_files and cached
   the computed value once on WatchSession at initialize().

Also fixed the same-shaped bug in Phase 3.5/3.6 themselves: both merged
freshly-parsed .d.ts data into `global` without draining its
diagnostics first, silently losing anything the extractor flagged
while parsing @types/react or a lib.d.ts file specifically (an
excessive-nesting trip, a parse error). Extracted the shared
merge_cached_dts_file helper, used by both phases, which drains first.

Two pre-existing tests encoded the old (incorrect) assumption that
update_file's affected_files/diagnostics keys would exactly echo a
raw, non-canonicalized input path — updated to canonicalize the
comparison value instead of the behavior under test.

fix(cli): fix --json exit codes, scope the flag honestly, stop silently defaulting react-version

Adversarial review found --json was broken in three ways:

1. extract --json returned before the error-diagnostic exit-code
   check, so it always exited 0 even on hard errors — the one signal
   CI actually depends on. Fixed by refactoring cmd_extract/cmd_check
   to return the intended exit code as a value instead of calling
   std::process::exit() deep inside business logic — makes the
   decision testable (added a real regression test) and lets main() be
   the only place that actually terminates the process.

2. --json was a global clap flag, so `check`/`watch`/`inspect --help`
   all advertised it while silently ignoring it (only cmd_extract ever
   read it). Scoped it to a per-command field on ExtractArgs/CheckArgs
   instead: extract already had a natural machine-readable output to
   gate, and check's diagnostics were an easy, coherent fit to wire up
   for real. watch/inspect no longer claim to accept a flag that did
   nothing.

3. node/tsx subprocess stderr was sent to Stdio::null(), so a
   docgen.config.ts that failed to evaluate produced a generic "failed
   to evaluate (exit status: 1)" with the real syntax error/stack
   trace thrown away. Now piped and included in the error message.
   Also wrapped the spawn() failure itself with a clear "is node
   installed and on PATH?" message instead of a bare OS error.

Also fixed --react-version silently defaulting to react19 on any
unrecognized value (a typo, or a NAPI caller bypassing the

  canonicalize_first_src_dir(), each caller keeping its own fallback

# oxc-react-docgen

React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax.

> **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete.

## Why

`react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system this takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass, so cold extraction on a 15-component fixture set (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, Radix) takes **32ms**.

The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet.

## Install

`@oxc-react-docgen/napi`, `@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin`, and `@oxc-react-docgen/cli` are not yet published to npm — there are no per-platform prebuilt binaries to install today. Until a release ships:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/castrog/oxc-react-codegen
cd oxc-react-codegen
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi run build:napi   # builds the native addon for your platform
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
```

`pnpm run build:napi` (not a bare `cargo build`) matters: it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s generated loader expects it. This works as a monorepo-local dependency today; there are no published per-platform packages for it to fall back to yet. See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) if you're moving off `react-docgen-typescript` and want to know exactly what's compatible today.

## Vite plugin

// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { oxcReactDocgen } from '@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin'
export default defineConfig({
import docgen from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'

# crates/core

Pure extraction logic — no terminal, no NAPI, no async. Everything here must be `Send + Sync` for rayon.

## Module layout

```
types/          — shared data types (the contract between phases)
extractor/      — OXC AST visitor → SourceData
resolver/       — SourceData + GlobalSourceData → ComponentEntry
pipeline/       — orchestration: discover → parse → merge → resolve
cache.rs        — DTS parse cache (mtime+size invalidation, msgpack)
import_map.rs   — import resolution map
known.rs        — library-specific type shortcuts (SxProps, VariantProps…)
react_types.rs  — React builtin recognition + notable HTML attrs
```

## Types discipline

When adding a public type, run through the checklist in the `rust-types` skill. Canonical reference: `src/types/diagnostic.rs`.

## Resolver

# crates/cli

Thin command layer — no extraction logic. Each command parses args and delegates to `oxc-react-docgen-core::pipeline`.

## Layout

```
main.rs              — Cli struct, Command enum, *Args structs, main(), init_tracing()
commands/            — one file per subcommand (extract, watch, inspect, check, completions)
config.rs            — docgen.config.ts loading, maps to PipelineOptions
output.rs            — comfy-table formatting helpers
```

## Rules

All user-facing output goes through `output.rs` or the tracing subscriber — never `println!` in command handlers. Error display uses `miette`. Progress uses `indicatif`.

Config loading (`config.rs`) runs the user's `docgen.config.ts` via node+tsx. The config file path is passed via env var, not embedded in a shell string — command injection risk otherwise.

TypeScript 7.0 RC shipped 2026-06-18. This is the Go rewrite of the compiler ("tsgo"),
not a JavaScript refactor. The key changes:

- **TypeScript 6.0** = last JavaScript-based tsc (maintenance only)
- **TypeScript 7.0** = Go rewrite; 10× build speed, same semantics
- **Strada API** (ts.createProgram, checker.getTypeAtLocation, LanguageService) = **completely dropped** in TS 7.0 — no shim, no compatibility layer
- **react-docgen-typescript** depends on Strada; it is **broken under TS 7.0**

### Corsa API

The tsgo team is building "Corsa" as the replacement public API. Status:

- Corsa API: **not yet stable** — targeting TypeScript 7.1 (estimated late 2026 / early 2027)
- Current tsgo exports minimal surface: `check()`, `build()`, basic diagnostics
- No `getTypeAtLocation` equivalent yet
- Plugin system and language service extensions TBD

### tsgolint precedent (OXC team)

The OXC team already tackled cross-language integration with `tsgolint`:
- Spawns `tsgo` as a subprocess
- Communicates via JSON IPC using tsgo's internal (unstable) shims
- This pattern works but depends on internal APIs that will break when Corsa lands

We should NOT follow the tsgolint approach — it creates maintenance debt on an unstable
internal API. Wait for Corsa.

### Why oxc-react-docgen is unaffected by TS 7.0

We parse TypeScript with OXC (Rust), not tsc. We have no dependency on the Strada API.
Consumers running TS 7.0 can use oxc-react-docgen without any changes. This is a
competitive advantage during the TS 6→7 migration window.

---
name: rust-style
description: Apply when writing or modifying Rust code in this project.
---

**Goal:** Code correct by construction, readable under churn, performant in hot paths.

## Project-specific decisions

These are non-negotiables, not preferences:

- Internal maps: `FxHashMap`. JSON-output maps: `BTreeMap` (deterministic key ordering).
- Type/prop names: `CompactString` — avoids heap allocation for strings ≤24 bytes.
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?` and let callers decide what to do with failure.

## Control flow

`let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
let Ok(parsed) = input.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
```

## Matching

No wildcards — a compile error on unhandled variants is a feature:

```rust
match status { Status::Ok => .., Status::Err => .. }  // compiler tells you when Status grows
match status { Status::Ok => .., _ => .. }             // silently misses new variants
```

Full `match` over `matches!` for the same reason.

## Types

Newtypes when a bare type allows confusion. Enums when a bool parameter hides intent:

```rust
struct ScopedKey(CompactString);         // not: String
enum Visibility { Public, Private }      // not: is_public: bool
```

Explicit destructuring gets compiler errors when structs change:

```rust
let ComponentEntry { display_name, file_path, .. } = entry;
```

## Naming

Shadow variables through transformations — no `raw_`/`parsed_`/`trimmed_` prefixes:

```rust
let path = args.path;
let path = path.canonicalize()?;
let path = path.join("config.toml");
```

## Comments

Only when the WHY is non-obvious: a hidden constraint, a workaround, a non-obvious invariant. Not what the code does.

## Key GitHub Actions for moonrepo

There are two main GitHub Actions available for moonrepo CI workflows:

### 1. **setup-moon-action**
A GitHub action for installing moon globally and caching the toolchain. This action caches the moon toolchain at ~/.moon (or ~/.proto), keyed by hashing the .moon/toolchain.yml configuration file found in the repository.

### 2. **setup-toolchain**
A GitHub action to setup and cache the proto and moon toolchains, which hashes .prototools and .moon/toolchain.yml files to generate a unique cache key. This action conditionally installs moon globally if the repository is using moon (attempts to detect a .moon directory), or moon-version is set.

The setup-toolchain action includes an auto-install parameter to auto-install proto tools by running proto install.

## CI Workflow Usage
For GitHub, moonrepo recommends using their setup-toolchain action to install moon. Additionally, moonrepo suggests using their moonrepo/run-report-action for GitHub Actions CI, which will report the results of a moon ci run to a pull request as a comment and workflow summary.

## Full Configuration Schema

Oxfmt supports these top-level configuration keys:

**Formatting Options:**
- `arrowParens`, `bracketSameLine`, `bracketSpacing`, `embeddedLanguageFormatting`
- `endOfLine`, `htmlWhitespaceSensitivity`, `insertFinalNewline`
- `jsdoc`, `jsxSingleQuote`, `objectWrap`
- `printWidth` (line length setting; default: `100`)
- `proseWrap`, `quoteProps`, `semi`, `singleAttributePerLine`, `singleQuote`
- `sortImports`, `sortPackageJson`, `sortTailwindcss`
- `svelte`, `tabWidth`, `trailingComma`, `useTabs`, `vueIndentScriptAndStyle`

**Special Keys:**
- `ignorePatterns` - Glob patterns using gitignore-style matching
- `overrides` - File-specific configuration overrides

feat: add oxlint — pedantic for source, relaxed for tests, real findings fixed

No TS/JS linting existed anywhere in the repo before this (no eslint,
no oxlint). Enabled correctness/suspicious/pedantic/perf/style categories
for real source (packages/vite-plugin/src, napi's hand-maintained
index.d.ts, the cli npm wrapper, apps/validate/src) — genuinely strict,
not just the default correctness-only baseline.

oxlint's config format can't scope *categories* per file glob (overrides
only support individual `rules`, confirmed against its own schema) — so
the "relaxed for tests" split happens via two separate invocations with
CLI category flags (-A pedantic -A perf -A style for tests), not a
config-file override. The override block still adds the vitest plugin
for test files and turns off node/no-sync for the two genuinely
one-shot script contexts (apps/validate's CLI scripts, the cli npm
wrapper) where blocking sync I/O is correct, not a mistake — a rule
written for long-running servers doesn't fit a script that runs once
and exits.

Turned off ~19 rules that were pure noise against this codebase's actual
conventions rather than real quality signal: no-magic-numbers flagged
every numeric literal, id-length fought the codebase's deliberate short
names, sort-keys/sort-imports/sort-vars have no real value, curly/
no-ternary/func-style are house-style opinions that fought existing
code, capitalized-comments/no-inline-comments/require-unicode-regexp
are niche nitpicks. Checked what remained across ~130 findings, then
fixed each real one: two instances of genuine dead code (an unused
`normalize` function, an unused `mkdirSync` import), 3 unused imports,
a nested ternary refactored into an if-else chain, inconsistent catch
variable names, array callback references needing explicit wrapping,
a negated condition, direct member access converted to destructuring,
and a useless `?? []` fallback on a Set constructor.

Two findings were false positives for a specific, deliberate reason,
not real issues: vite-plugin's configureServer hook must return its

### 1. `follow_reexports` has no visited-set — barrel graphs blow up exponentially
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/crates/core/src/resolver/import.rs:51-82`

**What it is.** The newly wired barrel/re-export resolution recurses through every `export * from` specifier with only `depth >= MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH` (8) as a bound. No `(file, name)` visited tracking, no memoization anywhere upstream — `resolve_to_canonical` is called fresh from `chain.rs:143`, `named.rs:47`, `primitives.rs:138`, `substitute.rs:93`, `template.rs:116`, and `ResolutionContext` (`resolver/mod.rs:96-121`) holds no cache. Cyclic or diamond-shaped barrel graphs therefore re-walk the same subtree once per path, `branching_factor^depth`.

Reproduced empirically with N mutually-re-exporting barrel files plus one component importing a name that doesn't exist (the unhappy path, which forces full traversal every call):

| N barrels | `pipeline::extract` wall |
|---|---|
| 2 | 156 ms |
| 4 | 188 ms |
| 5 | ~550 ms |
| 6 | 2.52 s |
| 7 | 9.70 s |

**Why it matters here.** Seven files turn a ~150 ms extraction into 9.7 s. The entire pitch is "32 ms cold vs RDT's multi-second spin-up"; this hands that back on a graph shape (`index.ts` wildcarding into sub-barrels that share an internal `types.ts`) that is *the exact motivating case* for the feature per the doc comment at `import.rs:44-50`. The non-cyclic diamond case degrades polynomially with no cycle needed at all. Every other recursive resolver walk in this codebase already guards this way (`chain.rs:39` `state.visited.insert(visit_key)`, `alias.rs:46-52` branch-local visited clone) — `follow_reexports` is the lone exception.

**Secondary accuracy consequence (non-negotiable #6 adjacent):** `resolve_import_specifier` pushes an `UnresolvableImport` diagnostic per failure (`import.rs:196-204`), and nothing dedupes diagnostics in `pipeline/mod.rs`. Repeated traversal of the same failing edge emits N duplicate user-visible diagnostics for one real problem.

**Fix.** Thread `visited: &mut FxHashSet<(Utf8PathBuf, CompactString)>` through `follow_reexports` and skip already-seen pairs; this subsumes the depth cap and collapses the redundant work. Fold in the memoization case below with the same change — a per-`ResolutionContext` memo of `(file, name) -> (canonical_file, canonical_name)` measured ~4x redundant `resolve_import_specifier` calls (4080 → 1014 on a 40-component fixture, `follow_reexports` CPU 14.5 ms → 6.6 ms, ~5-6% wall) even with a crude contended mutex. Two constraints on that memo: it must not swallow the `UnresolvableImport` diagnostics `resolve_import_specifier` emits, and `ResolutionContext` is shared by `&` across rayon, so it needs interior mutability that doesn't reintroduce lock contention (per-resolution-call memo in `ResolveState` avoids the problem entirely if cross-component reuse isn't worth the sharding work).

While in here: `is_declared_at` (`import.rs:87-92`) does up to four `format!` allocations per visit, and `ImportResolutionMap::resolve_reexport_chain` (`import_map.rs:94-115`) rebuilds a `Vec` of cloned specifier `String`s on every call. Both are cheap to fix once the traversal count is bounded.

fix(resolver): stop barrel resolution from exploring branching_factor^depth calls

Adversarial review (Opus 5 + Fable 5 verifying Sonnet 5's findings)
caught a real P0: follow_reexports had MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH as a recursion
bound but no visited-set, so a barrel graph where multiple parents
wildcard-re-export the same shared descendant — several sub-barrels all
wildcarding a common types.ts, ubiquitous in real component libraries —
re-explores that shared subtree once per path into it. Reviewer-measured
with real distinct files: 7 barrels took 9.7s wall time vs 156ms at 2.
This directly undermines the project's entire pitch (32ms cold
extraction vs RDT's multi-second Program spin-up) on exactly the graph
shape the barrel-resolution feature was built for.

Fixed by threading a visited: FxHashSet<(Utf8PathBuf, CompactString)>
through the traversal — skip a (file, name) pair already explored from
a different parent. This also subsumes cycle detection (a cycle
revisits a pair by definition), though the depth cap stays as a second
line of defense.

graph deep enough to hit MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH, querying a name that's
never declared anywhere so the unhappy path forces full traversal
instead of an early exit). Wall-clock time turned out not to be a
reliable signal for a fast unit test — oxc_resolver's own path cache
and this codebase's cheap per-call work meant even the unfixed version
ran under a second here. Added a #[cfg(test)]-only call counter instead
and asserted on it directly: 511 calls without the fix (confirmed by
temporarily disabling just the visited-set check), 9 with it — matching
the reviewers' predicted branching_factor^depth vs linear-in-graph-size
difference exactly.

fix(ci): fix moon affected-detection — it never actually ran, plus a gating hole it was masking

Adversarial review (Opus 5 + Fable 5) caught that moon 2.3.3's `query
projects` has no --base/--head flags at all (confirmed against its own
--help). The literal command in b06e303 failed immediately with a clap
parse error, which both fail-open branches then caught — so every CI
run since that commit landed has silently taken the "moon query failed
— running everything" path. The affected-detection feature never once
engaged; it fails open by design, so nothing was WRONGLY skipped, but
the commit's stated benefit (skip untouched language groups) was dead
on arrival.

Fixed by reading the base from MOON_BASE (moon's actual mechanism,
verified empirically: same-commit base+head returns zero affected
projects on a clean tree, a dirty single-file edit attributes correctly
to exactly the right project, and a real 34-commit range with genuine
Rust changes correctly flags both language groups). Also verified
MOON_HEAD is silently ignored — moon always diffs against whatever's
currently on disk, which is exactly github.sha here since
actions/checkout already put us there, so there's nothing to fix about
that, just a misleading comment to correct.

Fixing #1 without a second change would have opened a real gating hole
that the dead detection was accidentally masking: the category-mapping
loop had arms for core/cli/crates-binding (rust) and vite-plugin/napi
(typescript) but nothing for `validate` (apps/validate) or
`packages/cli` — the latter wasn't even registered as a moon project at
all, despite being explicitly linted/formatted by the `format` job. A
PR touching only apps/validate/src or packages/cli/bin/cli.js — the
exact tree 31fd9f5 hand-edited for lint fixes — would have gotten zero

# 0002. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-07-22 (retroactive)

## Context

`PropType` and `CollectedType` are recursive enums — variants nest through `Vec`/`Box`/`Option` back into the same type (`Union`, `Object`, `Array`, ...). At some point this project derived `Serialize`/`Deserialize` directly on a tagged `PropType` (`#[serde(tag = "kind")]`) and had to raise `#![recursion_limit]` to 2048 to get it to compile — each nesting level wraps the generated serializer in another layer during codegen, and the default limit (128) isn't enough for a real component tree.

## Decision

`PropType`, `CollectedType`, and `OpaqueReason` don't derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize`. Each has a hand-written impl (`to_json_value`/`from_json_value` for the first two) that builds a `serde_json::Value` directly instead of going through serde's derive machinery.

## Consequences

- Adding a new variant means updating the manual match in both directions by hand — the compiler won't remind you the way a derive would. `resolver/mod.rs`'s "no wildcard matches" convention is what catches a missed arm here instead.
- `CollectedObjectField` (a struct nested inside `CollectedType::Object`, not an enum) still derives normally — the recursion problem is specific to the recursive *enums*, not every type that touches them.
- The `#![recursion_limit = "2048"]` attribute in `crates/core/src/lib.rs` is left over from the old derive-based design. Verified 2026-07-22: the full workspace builds and every test passes with it removed — nothing in the current manual-impl code path needs it. Worth deleting as a follow-up; left as-is here since confirming that wasn't the point of this decision.

## Alternatives considered

`serde(remote)`, or just keeping the recursion-limit bump — both keep the derive, so you inherit the compile-time cost and a cryptic "recursion limit exceeded" the moment someone adds one more level of nesting. Manual impls trade a bit of hand-maintenance for a predictable compile time.

### `FxHashMap` over `HashMap`

OXC uses `FxHashMap` throughout. For short keys (type names, file paths) the FNV-derived hash in `rustc-hash` is faster than SipHash with no DoS-relevant surface for this use case.

### `CompactString` for type and prop names

Most names in the hot path (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`, `className`) are ≤24 bytes. `CompactString` stores them inline without heap allocation. Extraction visits thousands of names per file; this adds up.

### Manual `Serialize`/`Deserialize` for `CollectedType` and `PropType`

Both are deeply recursive enums. `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` hit Rust's monomorphization recursion limit during macro expansion, producing 19-minute compile times. Both now implement serialization manually through `serde_json::Value` as an intermediate, which breaks the recursion chain at the cost of one heap allocation per serialized value. A `#![recursion_limit = "2048"]` attribute is still present in `lib.rs` for other traits but is no longer load-bearing for these types.

### DTS cache location: `node_modules/.cache/`

`.d.ts` files from `node_modules` rarely change within a project session. The cache stores parsed `SourceData` keyed by file path, mtime, and size, serialized with msgpack and written atomically. `node_modules/.cache/` is the correct location: it is cleaned with `node_modules`, excluded from version control, and preserved across CI runs when `node_modules` is cached by layer.

1	# oxc-react-docgen
2	
3	React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax.
4	
5	> **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete.
6	
7	## Why
8	
9	`react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system this takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass, so cold extraction on a 15-component fixture set (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, Radix) takes **32ms**.
10	
11	The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet.
12	
13	## Install
14	
15	`@oxc-react-docgen/napi`, `@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin`, and `@oxc-react-docgen/cli` are not yet published to npm — there are no per-platform prebuilt binaries to install today. Until a release ships:
16	
17	```bash
18	git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/oxc-react-docgen
19	cd oxc-react-docgen
20	pnpm install
21	pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi run build:napi   # builds the native addon for your platform
22	pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
23	```
24	
25	`pnpm run build:napi` (not a bare `cargo build`) matters: it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s generated loader expects it. This works as a monorepo-local dependency today; there are no published per-platform packages for it to fall back to yet. See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) if you're moving off `react-docgen-typescript` and want to know exactly what's compatible today.
26	
27	## Vite plugin
28	
29	```ts
30	// vite.config.ts
31	import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
32	import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
33	import { oxcReactDocgen } from '@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin'
34	
35	export default defineConfig({
36	  plugins: [
37	    react(),
38	    oxcReactDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] }),
39	  ],
40	})
41	```
42	
43	Metadata is available on the `virtual:oxc-react-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change:
44	
45	```ts
46	import docgen from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'
47	
48	docgen.components['Button'].props
49	// {
50	//   variant: {
51	//     type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true },
52	//     required: false,
53	//     defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false },
54	//     description: '',
55	//   },
56	//   ...
57	// }
58	```
59	
60	## CLI
61	
62	The CLI is a single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and
63	`--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there and nowhere else.
64	`@oxc-react-docgen/cli` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that just execs the platform-appropriate compiled binary; it deliberately contains no reimplementation of CLI behavior, so there's exactly one place that behavior can drift.
65	
66	```bash
67	# Once published: npx @oxc-react-docgen/cli extract --src src/ --out docgen.json
68	# From source today: ./target/release/oxc-react-docgen (after cargo build --release)
69	
70	# One-shot extraction
71	oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json
72	
73	# Inspect a single file
74	oxc-react-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx
75	
76	# Watch mode
77	oxc-react-docgen watch --src src/
78	
79	# Shell completions
80	oxc-react-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_oxc-react-docgen
81	
82	# Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset
83	oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full
84	```
85

        lines = fh.read().split('\n')

    out = []
    in_code = False
    para = []

    def flush():
        if not para:

        is_list_like = all(
            l.lstrip().startswith(markers) or re.match(r'^\d+\.', l.lstrip())
            for l in para if l.strip()

        if len(para) > 1 and not is_list_like and not all_hard_break:

        else:

        if stripped == '':
            flush()
            out.append(line)
            continue
        para.append(line)
    flush()

    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        fh.write(new_content)
